definitions.gloss: to make plans; to set up a schedule; to plan ahead
definitions.explanation: To create or arrange a plan or schedule for future activities. The verb {立|た}てる here means to set up or establish.

examples.japanese: ⟦{旅行|りょこう}→旅行：00748_ryokou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{予定|よてい}を{立|た}てた。
examples.english: I made plans for a trip.

examples.japanese: ⟦{来週|らいしゅう}→来週：00746_raishuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{予定|よてい}を{立|た}てておこう。
examples.english: Let's go ahead and make plans for next week.

examples.japanese: ⟦{早|はや}め→早め：11176_hayame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{予定|よてい}を{立|た}てない⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦ホテル→ホテル：01027_hoteru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{取|と}れなく→取れる：02376_toreru⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: If we don't plan ahead early, we won't be able to get a hotel.

examples.japanese: ⟦{仕事|しごと}→仕事：00480_shigoto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{忙|いそが}しくて→忙しい：00591_isogashii⟧、⟦なかなか→なかなか：01547_nakanaka⟧{予定|よてい}を{立|た}てられない。
examples.english: I'm so busy with work that I can hardly make any plans.

notes:
A common collocation pairing ⟦{予定|よてい}→予定：00824_yotei⟧ ('plan, schedule') with ⟦{立|た}てる→立てる：01196_tateru⟧ ('to set up, establish'). This is the standard way to express making plans or setting a schedule in Japanese. The verb ⟦{立|た}てる→立てる：01196_tateru⟧ is ichidan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{旅行|りょこう}→旅行：00748_ryokou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{予定|よてい}を{立|た}てる: to plan a trip
- ⟦{勉強|べんきょう}→勉強：00770_benkyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{予定|よてい}を{立|た}てる: to make a study plan
- ⟦{年間|ねんかん}→年間：00974_nenkan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{予定|よてい}を{立|た}てる: to set up a yearly schedule
- ⟦{無理|むり}→無理：01558_muri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧{予定|よてい}を{立|た}てる: to make a reasonable plan

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{計画|けいかく}→計画：01172_keikaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{立|た}てる→立てる：01196_tateru⟧: to make a plan — more formal and often used for larger, more structured plans
- ⟦{日程|にってい}→日程：04289_nittei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{決|き}める→決める：00858_kimeru⟧: to set a schedule — focuses on fixing dates
- ⟦{段取|だんど}り→段取り：06629_dandori⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つける→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧: to make arrangements — emphasizes practical preparation steps

USAGE:
In everyday conversation, {予定|よてい}を{立|た}てる is the most natural way to talk about planning. It can refer to anything from casual weekend plans to structured work schedules.
